tables.table_description: Staff directory for the retail business. Each row represents one employee, linked to a single store and carrying their role (Cashier, Inventory Clerk, or Store Manager), hire date, and contact email. Used to attribute sales transactions to the serving employee.

columns.name: inventory_id

columns.name: product_id

columns.name: quantity_on_hand
columns.column_description: Current stock count (in units) of the product available at the store. Ranges from 35 to 120 in observed data.

columns.name: reorder_level
columns.column_description: Minimum stock threshold (in units) that triggers a replenishment order. When quantity_on_hand falls to or below this level, restocking should be initiated.

columns.name: last_restocked_at
columns.column_description: UTC timestamp of the most recent stock replenishment event for this product at this store. Nullable — null indicates the product has never been restocked since tracking began.

columns.name: created_at
columns.column_description: UTC timestamp of when the inventory record was first inserted into the database.

columns.name: updated_at
columns.column_description: UTC timestamp of the most recent update to the inventory record, such as a stock quantity adjustment.

tables.table_description: Per-store stock position table. Each row represents the current inventory level for one product at one store, including the quantity on hand, the reorder threshold, and the last restocking timestamp. Used to drive replenishment workflows and stock availability reporting.

columns.name: product_id
columns.column_description: Unique surrogate identifier for each product, auto-incrementing bigint primary key.

columns.name: supplier_id
columns.column_description: Foreign key referencing suppliers.supplier_id — the primary supplier that sources this product.

columns.name: sku
columns.column_description: Stock-keeping unit code — a short, human-readable product identifier (e.g. APL-001, TEA-001). Unique per product.

columns.name: name
columns.column_description: Full product display name as shown to staff and customers (e.g. 'Apples Gala 1kg', 'Whole Milk 1L').

columns.name: category
columns.column_description: Product category used for grouping and reporting. Known values: 'Bakery', 'Dairy', 'Grocery', 'Produce'. No database constraint enforces this set.

columns.name: unit_price
columns.column_description: Retail selling price per unit charged to customers, stored as numeric(10,2) in the local currency (EUR).

columns.name: cost_price
columns.column_description: Supplier cost price per unit paid by the business, stored as numeric(10,2) in the local currency (EUR). Used for margin calculations.

columns.name: active
columns.column_description: Soft-delete flag. True indicates the product is currently available for sale; false means the product has been deactivated. Filter on active = true to retrieve the current product catalogue.

columns.name: created_at
columns.column_description: UTC timestamp of when the product record was first inserted into the database.

columns.name: updated_at
columns.column_description: UTC timestamp of the most recent update to the product record, such as a price or category change.

tables.table_description: Product catalogue for the retail business. Each row describes a sellable item with its SKU, display name, category (Bakery, Dairy, Grocery, Produce), retail unit price, supplier cost price, and active status. Inactive products (active = false) are soft-deleted and should be excluded from current catalogue queries.

tables.table_description: Line-item detail for supplier purchase orders. Each row represents one product line within a purchase order, capturing the product ordered, the quantity, and the agreed unit cost at the time of ordering. Joins to purchase_orders for header-level context (supplier, store, status, dates).

columns.name: supplier_id

columns.name: store_id
columns.column_description: Foreign key referencing stores.store_id — the store that raised and will receive this purchase order.

columns.name: status
columns.column_description: Lifecycle status of the purchase order. Known values: 'Approved' (order confirmed with supplier), 'Received' (goods delivered). No database constraint enforces this set.

columns.name: order_date
columns.column_description: Business date on which the purchase order was raised with the supplier. Not safe as an incremental watermark — use created_at instead, as order_date can lag record insertion by up to ~96 days.

columns.name: expected_date
columns.column_description: Expected delivery date agreed with the supplier. Nullable — null indicates no confirmed delivery date has been set.

columns.name: created_at
columns.column_description: UTC timestamp of when the purchase order record was first inserted into the database.

columns.name: updated_at
columns.column_description: UTC timestamp of the most recent update to the purchase order, such as a status change.

tables.table_description: Line-item detail for customer sales transactions. Each row represents one product sold within a sales order, capturing the product, the quantity sold, and the unit price at the time of sale. Joins to sales_orders for header-level context (store, customer, employee, order date, status, total).

columns.name: sales_order_id
columns.column_description: Unique surrogate identifier for each sales transaction, auto-incrementing bigint primary key.

columns.name: store_id
columns.column_description: Foreign key referencing stores.store_id — the store where the transaction took place.

columns.name: customer_id
columns.column_description: Foreign key referencing customers.customer_id — the customer who placed the order. Nullable to allow anonymous (walk-in) sales not tied to a registered customer.

columns.name: employee_id
columns.column_description: Foreign key referencing employees.employee_id — the employee who processed or attended the sale.

columns.name: order_date
columns.column_description: UTC timestamp of when the customer placed or completed the order. Use created_at as the preferred incremental watermark; order_date may lag by up to 24 hours.

columns.name: status
columns.column_description: Lifecycle status of the sales order. Known values: 'Completed' (transaction finalised), 'Pending' (awaiting payment or fulfilment). No database constraint enforces this set.

columns.name: total_amount
columns.column_description: Denormalised sum of all line-item totals for the order, stored as numeric(12,2) in EUR. Should equal the sum of (quantity * unit_price) across related sales_order_items rows.

columns.name: created_at
columns.column_description: UTC timestamp of when the sales order record was first inserted into the database. Preferred watermark column for incremental ingestion.

columns.name: updated_at
columns.column_description: UTC timestamp of the most recent update to the sales order, such as a status change.

tables.table_description: Header-level sales transaction records. Each row represents a single customer purchase at a store, processed by an employee. Captures the order datetime, lifecycle status (Pending / Completed), and the denormalised total amount. Line-item detail is in sales_order_items. The customer_id is nullable, allowing anonymous walk-in transactions.
